scenarios.title: Repair applications that read the wrong storage
scenarios.summary: Diagnose observed device references and save each application’s own original data source.
scenarios.objective: Save a recommended name-based device reference for Report reader to original north-data/daily-report. Save a recommended name-based device reference for Audit reader to original north-data/audit-copy. Keep the unrelated watch reference unchanged. Keep every original storage name, allocation, filesystem, file, PV membership and availability unchanged; create no extra storage. Verify both applications read their own original data and leave no unsaved reference edits.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read each application reader and failed check separately. A readable path can still point to the wrong volume. Edit and Save the affected reference, then check again; renames do not update application fields automatically.

lesson.prerequisite_note: You have inspected pvs/vgs/lvs, renamed original LVM objects and used the virtual file reader. Here you also edit the supplied application references; Save changes configuration and Check work grades its actual target.

concepts.title: A saved reference tells an application where to read
concepts.text: A device reference is text in application configuration. In this simulator the reader follows that saved path to one supplied LV and its /keep.txt record. Typing a draft changes nothing until Save. Check work verifies the actual original object and data, not just a readable path.

concepts.title: Group and volume are separate names
concepts.text: The recommended application form is /dev/VG/LV: /dev/sample-store/notes-v1 names notes-v1 inside sample-store. Hyphens stay single inside these two components. Use lvs to identify the current group and LV before editing.

concepts.title: Recognize an observed mapper name
concepts.text: An existing /dev/mapper/sample--store-notes--v1 uses doubled hyphens within each component and a single separator between group and LV. This is current internal encoding, not a stable application interface. Diagnose supplied old names, then prefer /dev/VG/LV; real dmsetup splitname can inspect current encoding but is not simulated here.

concepts.title: Readable is not necessarily correct
concepts.text: Report reader needs notes-v1; Audit reader needs review-copy. Both can read a real record even when Audit points to the report by mistake. Compare the application purpose and actual record before checking.

lesson.description: Worked example: sample-store has notes-v1 for Report reader and review-copy for Audit reader. Both initial mapper references read notes-v1. Inspect lvs, save each recommended canonical reference, then verify two different original records. Keep the unrelated watch reference unchanged.
lesson.try_change: After the worked example, change Audit reader to /dev/sample-store/notes-v1 and Save. It remains readable but Check separate example identifies the wrong original object. Restore review-copy and check again.

worked.explanation: Inspect sample-store and distinguish notes-v1 from review-copy. The readers below use their own saved paths, not the selected LV in the storage inspector.
Use the recommended /dev/VG/LV form for Report reader, Save, and compare the actual original record.
Audit reader initially reads the wrong original record. Save its own correct reference; readable alone is not enough.

hints: A readable reader may still use the wrong LV. Compare each application purpose with the original names in the task.
The recommended application form has three components: /dev, group and volume. Do not copy internal doubled hyphens into the canonical form.
Typing leaves saved configuration unchanged. Save each changed reference, then read its actual result and check all requirements.
scenarios.explanation: Two name-based references now resolve to their distinct original objects and retained data. The watch configuration and all storage remain unchanged. Internal mapper encoding helped diagnose the initial state; recommended application references use /dev/VG/LV.
scenarios.simplifications: Bounded virtual LVM objects, application configuration fields and flat virtual file readers only. /dev/VG/LV is the recommended name-based application interface; the modeled simple /dev/mapper encoding is current internal syntax, not a stable ABI. Internal object identifiers are simulator identity, not LVM UUIDs. At most four applications and one supplied open consumer. No host files/devices, kernel, udev, symlinks, mounts, fstab, boot updates, dmsetup command, UUID/LABEL references or shell execution. Renames preserve data but do not rewrite application references. Reports remain explicitly fixed simulator tables with byte counts and ModelActive.

scenarios.title: Restore application access after a storage handover
scenarios.summary: Rename existing storage, repair stale application references and verify retained data.
scenarios.objective: Rename original store-main to records-main and its original ledger-old LV to ledger-live. Save recommended name-based references so Report reader follows the original ledger data and Audit reader follows the original audit-copy data at their current names. Keep all original allocations, filesystem data, PV memberships and availability, including the live peer and inactive reserve, unchanged. Do not create, remove, grow or format storage. Verify both actual reader results and leave no unsaved reference edits.
scenarios.retry_guidance: Read each application reader and failed check separately. A readable path can still point to the wrong volume. Edit and Save the affected reference, then check again; renames do not update application fields automatically.

lesson.prerequisite_note: You have inspected pvs/vgs/lvs, renamed original LVM objects and used the virtual file reader. Here you also edit the supplied application references; Save changes configuration and Check work grades its actual target.

concepts.title: Storage identity survives a rename
concepts.text: A rename changes the original object’s name, not its extents or file data. A replacement LV with the same spelling is not the same object. Use the existing supported lvrename and vgrename commands, not create/copy/delete.

concepts.title: Application text does not rename itself
concepts.text: The canonical /dev/VG/LV interface is recommended, but it still contains names. Renaming a group or LV makes an old saved name stale. The simulated reader will show unavailable until you edit and Save the corresponding application reference.

concepts.title: Repair every affected caller
concepts.text: Renaming demo-box changes references for both notes-old and review-copy. Renaming only notes-old affects that LV alone. Inspect each reader separately; do not assume the neighbor follows the new group automatically.

concepts.title: Verify the handover, not just the spelling
concepts.text: After the renames, save the new Report and Audit paths and read the original records. Their text still describes the original data; that is evidence of retention, not a reason to rewrite it. Real UUID, mount, boot and udev workflows are outside this simulation.

lesson.description: Worked example: rename demo-box to lesson-box and its original notes-old LV to notes-live. First inspect lvs and both readers. Rename the existing objects, observe stale saved application references, then Save Report reader and Audit reader at the new names. Verify the same original records and unchanged peer allocation.
lesson.try_change: After the worked example, save Report reader’s original /dev/demo-box/notes-old path. Read the unavailable error and check the example. Restore its current reference without undoing the correct storage handover.

worked.explanation: Inspect both current original LVs and their reader data before the handover.
Rename the same notes-old allocation to notes-live. Its old application reference now fails; no data was copied.
Rename the whole original group. Both old group references are now stale, including the unchanged peer LV name.
Save Report reader at the new group and LV names; inspect the retained original record.
Save Audit reader at the new group and unchanged review-copy name; check all outcomes.
